extracted.intended_audience: public librarians, philanthropists, civic reformers, and municipal policymakers planning free circulating libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and operational criteria for creating small, free circulating libraries and reading-rooms targeted to poor, densely populated urban districts; includes selection, access, location, staffing, outreach, and success metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free lending to all
rubrics_metrics.description: Books to be lent out free of expense to anybody and everybody who wished them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only requirement in the experimental library was that some reference should be given to satisfy the librarian that the borrower had a fixed residence. Emphasizes removing financial barriers (expense of membership) as an impediment to access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal identification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only requirement that some reference be given to satisfy the librarian that the borrower had a fixed residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This minimal barrier preserved broad access while giving librarians confidence about borrowers’ locality; used in an experimental New York library implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target poorest and most densely populated districts
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish small libraries located in the centers of the poorest and most thickly-settled districts of the city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to make books readily accessible to the portion of the population least likely to use large monumental libraries; placement strategy is central to reaching the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select books with reference to community needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The books are to be selected with special reference to the wants of each community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local tailoring of collections rather than one-size-fits-all; selection should consider the specific intellectual appetites and needs of the neighborhood served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude works of doubtful influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully excluding all works of doubtful influence for good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curation policy to avoid materials judged potentially harmful or morally questionable for the target communities; an explicit filtering standard in the trustees’ proposed system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach reading-rooms to circulating libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading-rooms would be attached to each circulating library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an on-site space for readers; reading-rooms increase accessibility for those who may not borrow books or who benefit from guided use and suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep libraries small to increase librarian attention
rubrics_metrics.description: As the libraries are to be small, readers will be able to receive more than the usual attention at the hands of the librarians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational scale guideline: smaller branches enable more personalized service and outreach to inexperienced or indifferent readers (target demographic: young persons ages 14–21, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bulletins to guide readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of bulletins — lists of works, or newspaper and magazine articles, upon the more important subjects which from time to time come before the public — has been continued, and the suggestions made in them are found to be quickly and generally used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outreach/curation practice: actively recommend reading through curated lists and topical bulletins to stimulate reading habits and guide patrons to useful material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure success by circulation and retention metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use circulation statistics and loss rates to evaluate performance (example: with ~4,000 available books, each volume circulated over seventeen times; 64% of circulation was fiction; only six volumes lost in a year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete metrics to assess impact and efficiency: per-volume circulation rate, proportion of fiction vs. non-fiction, reader counts, demographic usage (e.g., ages 14–21), and loss rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove every impediment to procuring books
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove every possible impediment to the procurement of books for the indifferent or less-motivated segments of the population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: a large portion of urban populations are hindered by cost, inconvenience, or indifference; to reach them, libraries must minimize membership cost, accessibility barriers, and other frictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good government should give reason precedence and limit corrupting influences
rubrics_metrics.description: The wise ordering of elective government should give public reason the upper hand, and reduce, as far as possible, the influence of passion, class interest, selfish ambition, faction, and corruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative standard for political systems: judge institutions by their ability to elevate public reason and to restrain partisan or corrupting motives; stated as the political hope of the world in the essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political parties should promote principles, not perpetual power
rubrics_metrics.description: Party is a body united for promoting by their joint endeavors the national interest upon some particular principle on which all are agreed (Edmund Burke definition quoted); parties that eliminate principles in favor of perpetuating power are defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess parties by whether they rally around and implement principles (good) versus whether they prioritize self-preservation and power (bad). The essay criticizes parties that treat questions of principle as 'unavailable' and therefore hollow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific spirit as a political corrective
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific spirit, by increasing knowledge and harmonizing opinions, tends to disconcert party arrangements and leads men to agreement, making them revolt against the insincerity of partisan politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a normative criterion, political arrangements should be evaluated by how well they encourage independent, truth-seeking thought and reduce factionalism; the advance of public intelligence is presented as a remedy for pernicious party government.
